notes_for_editor: Evidence is thin on primary sources: Light-House Board reports before 1891 are not in the corpus, so the 1854-1890 chronology (appropriations, 1861 destruction, 1886 earthquake, 1887 storm, 1889 move, 1893 hurricane) rests on LighthouseFriends (facts, own words) and should be checked against Light-House Board reports 1872-1890 and newspapers. Disagreements flagged in the text: NRHP calls the 1859 tower wooden (the notice says brick) and gives 136 ft (Board 1894: 121 ft); Johnson 1889 says eight-inch concrete foundation, LighthouseFriends eight-foot; water 35 ft from dwelling (ETV) vs 60 ft (LF) in 1887; bridges 1939 (ETV) vs 1941 (LF); Gaillard principal keeper 1926 (Lighthouse Digest) vs 1927 (USLHS); Peter Peterson principal vs first assistant. LighthouseFriends prints 'a six months in 1899' for the move, evidently 1889. The first-order lens on display is from Morris Island; the Friends' lens page title calls it 'the 1875 Fresnel Lens', which conflicts with the same page's text. The original 1875 second-order lens's fate was not found. The 1894 Board summary is cited by scan page 649 (printed page unverified). Page numbers for the 1892 (p.104) and 1896 (p.98) reports come from each report's own index and page headers, not verified on the scan image. NRHP OCR is poor; its quotes are single-line fragments. The Dec 1929 aeroplane landing is from Lighthouse Digest (own words). No newspapers searched (loc.gov searches did not return in time). Fact-check 2026-10-27: Bulletin item on the lighted buoy is in the 1 April 1934 issue and reports 27 March; tender's name is garbled in OCR and left out.
